- Teleoperation & robot learning. Set up and operate teleoperation systems, record high-quality demonstrations for imitation learning, and support reinforcement-learning workflows including sim-to-real validation.

- Demo setups & showcases. Build reliable demonstrators for trade fairs, customer visits and pilot projects that can run repeatedly under real-world conditions.

- Shop floor deployment. Take applications from the lab into production environments, addressing cycle times, safety, system interfaces and integration with existing automation.

- Feedback into development. Capture field findings, failure modes and product limitations and work with Product and Engineering to translate them into concrete improvements.

- Documentation & enablement. Document applications, integration procedures and test results, and support customers and partners during deployment.

title: Staff Product Manager: Agentic Discovery
description:
Staff Product Manager, Agentic Discovery 

About Us Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you've probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it. We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We're approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical. We're a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers' and coworkers' lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

Job Summary We're looking for a systems-minded, AI-native Staff Product Manager to help lead the next chapter of Constructor: Agentic Discovery. As commerce shifts toward agentic experiences, we're investing heavily in a portfolio of AI-powered surfaces — our AI Shopping Assistant, Product Insights Agent, Prism recommendations, and more to come — that change how shoppers discover products and how businesses run discovery.

This is a high-leverage, high-ambiguity role. You'll own two things at once: helping our agentic experiences scale from promising experiments into a repeatable, reliable engine, and giving the business teams who depend on them the same transparency and control over agentic experiences that they have today over traditional search.

You'll start by owning the business tooling and dashboards for agentic discovery — the experiences that let business teams see what our agents are doing, why, and to what effect, so they can execute faster and steer with confidence. Over time, your mandate grows to setting direction for the entire Agentic Discovery chapter: the on-site agentic experiences, the offsite/agentic surfaces, the integrations that connect them, and the agentic tooling underneath. This is a Staff role today with a clear path to Director as you take on chapter-wide leadership.

Agentic discovery at Constructor is fundamentally an AI and machine learning problem, so this role lives and breathes it. You'll partner closely with ML, engineering, design, and go-to-market to turn new agentic capabilities into experiences that ship, prove value, and stay under our customers' control — and serve as the connective tissue that aligns multiple teams behind one coherent vision for agentic discovery.

If you're excited about defining a brand-new category, being held to real usage and business outcomes, and giving businesses control over the AI experiences shaping their storefronts, this role is for you.

What You'll Do 

- Own business impact, not features. Drive measurable lift in usage and business outcomes — conversion, revenue, engagement — across Constructor's agentic experiences.

- Give businesses transparency and control. Build the dashboards and tooling that let business teams see what agentic experiences are doing, understand why, and steer them — closing the gap to the control they have in traditional search.

- Scale experimentation. Turn one-off agentic experiments into a repeatable, scalable way to launch, measure, and improve new agentic interfaces — cutting time-to-launch.

- Set chapter vision and strategy. Define the multi-quarter direction for Agentic Discovery — where we're heading and why — tie it to customer business outcomes, and rally teams behind it.

- Lead the business-tooling and dashboard experience first. Own its strategy and roadmap, and make agentic behavior and impact visible and actionable for business users.

- Orchestrate across surfaces. Unite on-site agentic experiences, offsite/agentic surfaces, and integrations behind one definition of agentic discovery success, so improvements compound instead of colliding.

- Turn AI capability into shipped experiences. Partner with ML and engineering to take agentic and LLM-powered experiences from idea to production, balancing quality, latency, cost, and reliability.

- Make success measurable. Define and instrument the metrics — go-live velocity, usage, engagement, business outcomes — that tell us whether agentic discovery is working.

- Keep it trustworthy. Treat explainability, control, and guardrails as first-class requirements so customers trust and adopt agentic experiences.

- Grow the mandate. Expand from business tooling into chapter-wide leadership across the full agentic portfolio and the integrations beneath it.

What Success Looks Like Within your first year, you will have:

- Shipped a dashboard and tooling experience that gives business teams real transparency into and control over Constructor's agentic experiences, adopted by internal teams and customers.

- Driven measurable lift in the usage and business impact (conversion, revenue) of agentic experiences across multiple customers.

- Stood up a repeatable process for launching and experimenting with new agentic interfaces, measurably shortening time-to-launch.

- Defined the core metrics for agentic discovery and made them visible in one place.

- Begun uniting the on-site, offsite, and integrations teams behind one coherent direction for the chapter.

What We're Looking For 

- Extensive product management experience (typically 8+ years) in AI/ML, agentic, search, or discovery products, including time operating at a senior or staff level.

- A track record of moving business metrics at scale — usage, conversion, revenue, engagement — not just shipping features, and of setting strategy across multiple teams.

- Experience building for business users/operators (merchandisers, category managers, or similar) — especially the tooling, dashboards, and controls they rely on.

- Strong AI/ML/LLM product depth — understands how agentic and LLM-powered experiences work and can reason about their tradeoffs (quality, latency, cost, reliability).

- Comfort with zero-to-one ambiguity and with scaling — able to experiment on brand-new interfaces and to build the repeatable process that turns them into a portfolio.

- A rigorous, measurement-first mindset that ties every experience back to usage and business outcomes.

- Excellent cross-functional leadership — able to align teams with different goals behind a shared definition of success, working shoulder-to-shoulder with ML, engineering, design, and go-to-market.

- A strong instinct for trust — treating transparency, control, and guardrails as core to whether agentic experiences succeed.

- Comfort setting direction where none exists yet, and leading through clarity and credibility rather than the org chart.

Benefits 

- Unlimited vacation time — we strongly encourage all of our employees to take at least 3 weeks per year.

- A competitive compensation package including stock options.

- Company-sponsored US health coverage (100% paid for employee).

- Fully remote team — choose where you live.

- Work-from-home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office.

- Apple laptops provided for new employees.

- Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year.

- Parental leave for qualified employees.

- Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact.

This position is fully remote — Constructor.io is a remote-first company.

As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome individuals of all backgrounds and provide equal opportunities to all applicants regardless of their education, diversity of opinion, race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or affiliation in any other protected group.

title: Technical Product Manager - DevEx
description:
Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it 

Your mission is to make it dramatically easier for our engineers to ship features and learn from them quickly, securely, and reliably. You'll aim for small-startup speed while meeting the quality bar of a large financial institution. Velocity here means removing friction and toil from the path between idea and learning, not asking people to work harder.

AI is a big part of the opportunity, and we're looking for a PM who is optimistic about its possibilities but pragmatic about what actually works. The goal is not to adopt the latest shiny AI tool; it's to deeply understand your internal users, experiment, and honestly evaluate what solves their problems, whether that's AI, process changes, or boring tooling that just works.

The Technical Product Manager - DevEx will:

- Lead a team of engineers with full ownership of how we deliver new features for our users and use AI solutions to remove impactful friction for our engineers and product managers.

- Define product goals, metrics, and roadmaps based on user needs and mission impact.

- Drive user research within our engineering and product teams.

- Write clear, compelling design docs and facilitate async, fast-moving decision-making.

- Over-communicate context, priorities, and decisions to ensure team alignment.

- Adjust priorities quickly based on feedback, experiments, or new learnings.

- Solve problems holistically, whether through product features, ops tooling or process changes.

In this role, you'll... 

- Own the developer experience holistically, including any internal or external tooling needed to support it.

- Research and implement solutions for how we can use AI to remove engineering and development friction. 

- Build your own prototypes to test ideas where possible.

- Relentlessly gather feedback (by talking to users and looking at data) to deeply understand the problem space and our engineers' and product managers' needs.

- Work from first principles to understand the engineers' and product managers' biggest problems and then figure out how our tooling should work to solve those problems.

- Prioritize the biggest problems blocking the engineers' and product managers' productivity and the impact on delivering value to our users fast and securely.

- Directly manage the DevEx team to help them grow in their careers, partnering with the Tech Lead, who will own the technical bar.

Key Details 

- This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (UK, Spain, USA (East Coast), Canada, Kenya and Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso

- Wave provides a yearly $1,200 stipend to support co-working meetups with teammates.

- Remote team members are expected to travel to our operational markets (e.g. Senegal or Côte d'Ivoire) at least once per year. Exceptions apply, but we've found this key to understanding our users and product.

- Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level and location, we offer a salary up to $237,500 USD, plus a generous equity package.

- Major benefits:

- Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents, and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country).

- 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance.

- Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days per year. 

- $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.

Requirements 

- Have 3+ years of product management experience and hands-on engineering background (you've shipped production code) or direct PM ownership of a developer experience, or developer productivity function.

- Proven success in overseeing all elements of the product development lifecycle, such as user research, design, implementation and evaluation.

- Speak fluent English

- Bonus if you:

- Have proven experience with successfully rolling out AI-based solutions in a larger org

- Have professional experience in a consumer fintech company

You might be a good fit if you 

- Resonate deeply with how we do product and have experience working that way. 

- Are continuously iterating on using AI in real workflows with honest evaluation.

- Are a strong communicator who can inspire and lead by influence.

- Are great at coordinating across teams and excel at communicating across multiple cultures.

- Take ownership for outcomes and do whatever you can to make them close to inevitable.

- Have strong instincts for asking questions that could move the needle.

- Have the courage and persistence to replan when feedback or new information arrives.

- Always listen with empathy but ruthlessly prioritize based on impact.

About Product at Wave 

Product has always been very important to us at Wave, starting from day one with two very strong product-minded founders. Product Managers play a central role in our organization, impacting large chunks of the company around them, similar to the founders they were shaped after years ago.

Our approach to building products may not be what you've seen in other places. Our processes are lightweight, informed by principles instead of methodologies and our PMs don't just manage backlogs full of polished tickets. Read our write-up on product at Wave! 

If you're excited to own a real problem end-to-end, set your own goals, and guide a team toward outcomes that matter for real people, you'll feel right at home here.

If that's you, we'd love to meet you.

Our team

- We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.

- We're deeply passionate about our mission of bringing radically affordable financial services to the people who need them most.

- We foster autonomy for our employees. You'll own your projects at every stage, from understanding the problem to monitoring your solution in production.

- We raised the largest Series A in Africa in 2021. Our world-class investors, include Founders Fund, Sequoia Heritage, Stripe, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator, and Partech Africa.

- We are on Y Combinator's top companies by revenue .

How to apply

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

We review applications frequently and recommend that you apply to the role that most closely aligns with your skills, experience and career goals.

Wave is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Business Development Representative
description:
A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $96 million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Being a BDR at incident.io means learning to sell from some of the best in the business, while representing a product and account team that make every conversation an easy one to be proud of.

What that looks like day to day 

Cold calling is the heart of this role, and most of our meetings get booked over the phone - not because it's easy, but because it's still the fastest way to build real trust with a prospect. We don't copy-paste templates, and we don't spam: every call and every piece of outreach is backed by careful research and planning alongside the AEs you partner with, so the person on the other end knows you're not a random dial.

We're founded by engineers, and that shows up in how BDRs work too, everyone gets unlimited Claude tokens, and our head of business development is a former RevOps leader himself, so there's a real emphasis on testing, measuring, and optimizing your own workflow like an engineer would, not just running the same script on repeat.

BDRs are the bench for our wider GTM team, and your progress here matters beyond just you, it's how we keep the whole GTM engine strong. The path to AE is real, and for those who put in the work, that next step can come faster than you'd expect elsewhere - with the strength of the peer group you're learning from making all the difference.

Who you are

- You've got a strong why. Whatever got you here - sport, a career switch, a BDR track record that deserved the promotion you didn't get last time, you know exactly what you're chasing, and that's what gets you through the hard days.

- Cold calling doesn't scare you. A "no" doesn't ruin your afternoon, it's just the next dial.

- You're genuinely curious about people. You want to know what's keeping a VP of Engineering up at night, not just whether they'll take a meeting.

- You can write. Not novels, just outreach someone actually wants to open and reply to.

- You run toward the hard thing. Given the choice between the easy route and the challenging one, you take the challenging one, because you know that's where the bigger payoff is.

- You're always looking for a better way to work, and that includes using AI properly, testing new tools and workflows, not just running the same playbook because it's familiar.

- Startup life suits you. Things change, the odd thing is on fire, and you're fine figuring it out as you go with people around to help.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

- Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover — we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

- Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

- First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

- Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

- Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

- Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

- Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

- Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

Integrate vehicle dynamics, control laws, sensors, and actuators into a coherent closed‑loop system representation. 

- 
Identify system‑level risks early particularly around requirements gaps, controllability, observability, and verification — and drive mitigations decisively.

Act as a technical authority across disciplines, keeping architectural decisions coherent as designs evolve at pace.

An experienced Systems Engineer with a strong track record in system architecture, requirements decomposition, and delivery in safety‑ or mission‑critical environments.

Deeply fluent in model‑based systems engineering , with practical experience owning requirements models and using MBSE to drive real engineering decisions. 

- 
Strong grounding in closed‑loop control theory , applied to high‑speed flight, guidance, and defence or military systems. 

- 
Comfortable developing and working with 6‑DoF flight and GNC models , and understanding their implications at vehicle level. 

- 
Experienced taking systems through early design gates (Kick‑off, PDR), not just theoretical or paper studies. 

- 
Someone who thinks in system behaviours , interfaces, and failure modes , not isolated components. 

-

-

What we offer

A mission driven environment with the opportunity to work on one of Europe’s most consequential defence challenges, with direct impact on sovereign capability and security. 

- 
Daily collaboration with top experts across engineering, operations, and defence , with real opportunity to learn from the best, contribute, and grow. 

- 
High ownership and autonomy; no time tracking, no micromanagement , just clear objectives and accountability for outcomes. 

- 
A fast paced environment where good ideas are implemented quickly, and feedback from test and flight drives real decisions. 

- 
A culture that values clarity, integrity, and excellence, and supports people who take initiative and push boundaries responsibly. 

- 
Competitive compensation and real share options aligned to responsibility and impact, not tenure or hierarchy. 

At Hypersonica, every hire raises the bar. We are deliberately small, intensely capable, and deeply mission-driven. If this role feels like a strong fit, or if you believe you bring something exceptional that goes beyond the description, we encourage you to apply.

About the role 

Senior Engineering Managers at GitLab own outcomes for a defined engineering domain, build and grow the team that delivers them, and are trusted to operate with significant autonomy against a clear mandate.

This Senior Engineering Manager role focuses on driving non-linear productivity by building and leading a small, hand-picked team of engineers who find and fix the highest-leverage friction points in GitLab's own SDLC. Rather than incremental team management, this is a 0 to 1 team-building mandate. You will personally recruit 4 exceptional engineers, define how they work, and drive them through a root-cause, shift-left approach to engineering productivity, measured in system-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency), not story points or activity.

You will act as a bridge between the pilot squad, engineering managers whose teams are affected by friction points, and leadership, ensuring the team's fixes deliver durable, measurable value before any of it is proposed as a permanent function.

This role reports to a VP-level engineering leader.

What you'll do 

Vision & Strategy

- Define and continuously refine the operating model for the non-linear productivity pilot: what "friction" means, how it's diagnosed, and how fixes are prioritized against the three system-level metrics.

- Identify and prioritize non-linear productivity opportunities (step-change fixes rather than incremental gains) across the SDLC, including flaky tests, review latency, pipeline reliability, tooling gaps, and context loss for both human and agentic contributors.

- Translate an intentionally broad, ambiguous mandate ("find the friction, fix it at the root") into a concrete, time-boxed roadmap with defined milestones for a 3-month pilot window.

Team Building & Leadership

- Personally source, evaluate, and select 4 exceptional engineers for the pilot squad. You own this hiring bar directly rather than delegating it to a pipeline.

- Negotiate allocation models (100% vs. partial/dual-hat) with each engineer's current EM, balancing team commitments against the pilot's needs.

- Set the technical direction and working norms for a small, fast-moving team: how work is scoped, how decisions get made, and how progress gets reported.

- Mentor the engineers on this team in root-cause diagnosis and shift-left thinking, raising the bar for rigor versus reaching for the nearest patch.

Deep Technical Exploration & Experimentation

- Lead hands-on investigation to instrument and baseline the three top-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency) so the org has an honest starting point before any fix is proposed.

- Diagnose the highest-leverage friction points dragging each metric down, and validate hypotheses with real data before committing team time to a fix.

- Design and implement fixes that compound, including shift-left quality changes, tooling investment, and better context and interfaces for both humans and agents, rather than one-off patches.

- Stay hands-on enough to review architecture, dig into pipeline internals, and unblock the team on hard technical problems directly.

Internal Adoption & Non-Linear Productivity

- Own a small set of high-impact friction areas as pathfinders, driving each from diagnosis through fix to measurable metric movement.

- Work directly with affected engineering teams to ensure fixes are trusted, adopted, and don't quietly get reverted or worked around.

- Track and report metric movement honestly, including when a bet didn't pay off.

- Capture and codify reusable patterns and playbooks so that fixes validated by this team can be adopted org-wide with minimal friction.

Operations, Risk & Enablement

- Set a cadence for reporting impact back to EM peers and leadership, framed around metric movement rather than activity.

- Ensure the pilot's fixes degrade gracefully and don't introduce new reliability risk into CI/CD systems that other teams depend on.

- Help define what "graduation" from pilot to permanent function looks like, and build the case (or the honest counter-case) based on results.

What you'll bring 

General

- Track record leading small, high-autonomy engineering teams, ideally in developer productivity, CI/CD, platform, or infrastructure reliability, measured on system-level outcomes rather than feature delivery.

- Deep comfort with CI/CD and build systems. You understand why pipelines flake, why they're slow, and what actually moves success-rate and latency numbers versus what just feels like progress.

- Demonstrated root-cause instinct and a bar for talent over headcount: you'd rather run understaffed than fill a seat with someone good-enough.

- Comfort operating under metrics-driven accountability, including publicly baselining a number and reporting honestly against it.

- Strong executive-level communication. This pilot has direct visibility to engineering leadership.

Nice to have

- Experience with agentic or AI-assisted development workflows, and a view on where human/agent friction shows up differently than pure human friction.

- Prior experience running a defined-window pilot or 0 to 1 initiative with explicit success criteria.

- Familiarity with GitLab's own CI/CD internals, or equivalent depth on another large-scale build/test system.

description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

About Okta for AI Agents 

Okta secures access for 20,000 organizations and billions of users. Okta for AI Agents extends that work to the agentic shift. Deploying an AI agent is not like deploying traditional software. You are putting professional work output into production, and it needs deep integration, continuous tuning, and change management. Every agent needs an identity, a scope, an audit trail, and a way to be shut down when it goes wrong. Most enterprises have not built this yet. We are.

We hire builders who see the cracks in enterprise agent identity that everyone else has learned to live with.

The Role 

You are the most senior technical field authority for agent identity at Okta. Where a Senior FDE owns the outcome inside one account, you own the patterns that every account and every FDE inherits. You take the hardest and most strategic deployments yourself, set the reference architecture the team builds from, and turn what the field learns into the direction the product takes.

You still write code. You also multiply the people around you, and you are the person product and engineering leadership call when an agent identity problem has no precedent.

Responsibilities 

- Own the reference architecture. Define the canonical agent identity, delegation, audit, and kill-switch patterns that Senior FDEs deploy across the portfolio, and keep them current as the standards and the product move.

- Lead the hardest accounts. Personally own the most strategic, regulated, or technically novel deployments, the ones where there is no playbook yet.

- Raise the technical bar. Review other FDEs’ architectures, coach senior customer engineers and your own team, and set the standard for what good looks like in the field.

- Shape the roadmap. Synthesize patterns across every account into a clear point of view, and work directly with product and engineering leadership to prioritize what ships next.

- Represent Okta as a technical authority. Brief CISO, CIO, and Chief AI Officer audiences, contribute to the standards and frameworks shaping agent identity, and carry the external technical voice.

- Resolve what others cannot. Step into the hardest technical and political situations across accounts and find the path forward.

- Set the standard for evals and observability. Define how the team measures authorization latency, scope sprawl, delegation anomalies, audit completeness, and kill-switch verification, so it scales beyond any single customer.

- Build the team’s leverage. Turn recurring field work into reusable modules, internal tooling, and enablement so the whole FDE function moves faster.

Requirements 

- Engineering depth. 10+ years shipping production software, with deep distributed systems and identity experience and a track record of staying hands-on while setting direction.

- Authority-level identity protocols. OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, RFC 8693 token exchange, act claims, CIMD and DCR, DPoP. Contribution to standards or open source is a plus.

- Deep agent security fluency. OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, plus MCP, A2A, ISO/IEC 42001, and the EU AI Act, with the judgment to apply them in HIPAA, FedRAMP, and SOC 2 environments.

- Expert fine-grained authorization. ReBAC and ABAC with policy engines (OPA, Cedar, OpenFGA, or equivalent), and command of the design tradeoffs at scale.

- Proven AI hands-on. Production integrations across the major agent platforms and MCP, and daily AI-native development.

- Force multiplier. A record of setting technical direction across multiple teams or accounts, and of mentoring senior engineers.

- Customer-facing authority. Credible from the IDE to the boardroom, trusted by CISOs and principal engineers alike, and steady when account politics get sharp.

- High agency, founder’s mindset. Applied to building a function, not just an account.

- Ability to travel , on occasion, up to 35%

We've spent the last three years transforming how our People Team operates. Now we're looking for someone to own the machine and work out what comes next! 

About the role 

We're looking for a People Operations Lead to own the operating layer of our People function, managing our People Operations Specialist and reporting directly to our People Director.

This is a slightly unusual brief, because we're looking for a very particular combination of experience.

First and foremost, you need to be an experienced, hands-on People Operations person. But you also need to have previously worked as an accountant, or have substantial professional accountancy experience.

And we mean accountancy specifically. Experience partnering with Finance, managing a People budget or processing payroll isn't the same thing.

Why such a specific combination? Because we've seen first-hand just how well it can work .

We've seen the value that a professional accountancy background can bring when combined with strong People Operations experience - financial discipline, an instinct for controls and data, and an analytical approach to understanding how systems and processes work. We're now deliberately looking for that combination again.

This isn't a traditional HR Operations role, and we're not looking for someone to simply keep existing processes running. We want someone who's genuinely curious about how and why things work - someone who spots friction, interrogates the data, challenges the way we've always done things and builds something better.

You'll inherit a strong foundation. Over the last three years we've streamlined manual processes, invested in our People technology and changed the way our People function operates. There's plenty we're proud of - but we're definitely not done!

You'll own our People operations, systems and data infrastructure across the end-to-end colleague lifecycle, making sure the fundamentals run brilliantly while continuously looking for opportunities to simplify, automate and improve them.

You'll also take significant ownership of our reward infrastructure, including quarterly pay reviews, salary benchmarking and banding, benefits and gender pay gap reporting. You'll work closely with our People Partners, Talent, Finance, Payroll and Tech teams, so this is a highly collaborative role with influence across Goodlord.

And increasingly, you'll help us answer a bigger question: what work should technology be doing for us?

We're already exploring how AI and agentic workflows can remove repetitive work across areas such as onboarding, colleague queries, document management, data validation and reporting. You don't need to arrive as an AI expert, but you do need to be excited about the possibilities, willing to experiment and comfortable helping us work out where technology can genuinely make things better.

If you get a kick out of taking something that already works, understanding it properly and making it simpler, smarter and better, we'd love to hear from you. 

Who are you? 

You're probably someone who sees People Operations a little differently.

You care about delivering a brilliant colleague experience, but you're just as interested in the systems, data and processes underneath it.

You don't accept a seven-step process because it's always had seven steps. You'll want to understand why it's there, whether we still need it and what would happen if we did it differently.

What does that mean in practice? 

- You're naturally curious and analytical. You ask good questions, get underneath problems and use data rather than instinct alone to make decisions.

- You love improving how things work. You've reviewed, redesigned and implemented processes rather than simply inherited and administered them.

- You're comfortable getting into the detail while still seeing the bigger picture - whether that's interrogating a spreadsheet, configuring a workflow or digging into an HRIS.

- You're pragmatic, comfortable with ambiguity and a confident collaborator. You can turn an idea into something that actually works and bring people with you when something needs to change.

What we need from you

- Previous professional experience working as an accountant or in a substantive accountancy role. This is essential for this particular hire. 

- Significant People Operations experience, with evidence that you've owned and designed end-to-end People processes, not simply operated processes someone else created.

- Hands-on experience owning or significantly shaping People systems and data using a modern tech stack, including an HRIS (we use Personio, but we're of course open to others!) and/or headcount planning systems, alongside strong analytical and advanced Excel skills.

- Experience across reward and benefits, ideally including ownership of pay review cycles, salary benchmarking and banding, benefits and gender pay gap reporting.

- A track record of continuous improvement - spotting friction, getting underneath the root cause and leading meaningful changes that have made processes simpler, better or more scalable.

- An active interest in AI and automation and how they can change the way People teams operate. You'll be comfortable experimenting with new tools and ways of working.

- You'll be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment and working across People Partnering, Talent, Finance, Payroll and Tech to solve problems and make change happen.

It would also be great if you have 

- Experience working in a high-growth, scale-up or similarly fast-moving environment.

- Hands-on experience building or implementing AI/agentic workflows that are being used in practice.

And one thing you won't need 

A particular HR qualification. We care much more about what you've actually built, improved and owned than whether you have CIPD after your name.

A little more about the contract 

This is initially a three-month fixed-term contract. We're continuing to think about the longer-term shape of our People team, so there is the potential for the role to become permanent if there's a strong mutual fit and an ongoing need.

We're also open to part-time working for the right person. Finding the right combination of People Operations and professional accountancy experience matters more to us than insisting on a particular working pattern.

description:
Meet Arago and the Aragonians 

Arago’s mission is to re-engineer the foundations of computing from first principles.

The explosive growth of AI is pushing the industry to rethink how processors are built. Arago is meeting that challenge with a proprietary technology that fuses optical and CMOS technologies to deliver an order-of-magnitude increase in performance.

Arago is the fastest, and currently the only, company to have built such a processor. It's backed by leading deep-tech investors and some of the most respected figures in semiconductors and computing, including the CEO of Arm, the founder of macOS who worked directly with Steve Jobs at Apple, an Nvidia Fellow, the Head of Optics at Google, and many other industry leaders.

As Technical Sourcer at Arago, you will own the search for some of the most sought-after engineers in the world. We build hardware that has never existed before, and finding the people who can build it requires going far beyond standard recruiting channels.

You will own the full sourcing motion: mapping talent pools, building precise searches, crafting outreach that resonates with passive candidates, and building long-term relationships with high-priority profiles. Working directly with hiring managers and founders, you will develop a deep understanding of each role and the technical landscape around it, then go find the right people, wherever they are.

- Language: English at a proficient level.

We're Looking For 

- Proven sourcing experience in deep tech, semiconductors, or AI hardware, not just software 

- X-Ray search skills and comfort sourcing across GitHub, LinkedIn, and non-traditional channels

- Demonstrated success sourcing passive senior technical talent

- Ability to run multiple complex searches in parallel without dropping quality

- Genuine curiosity about the technology, you need to understand what you're sourcing for

- A long-game mindset: relationship building over transactional outreach

Nice to Have

- Proven track record of filling hard-to-find roles

- Experience writing outreach that actually gets replies

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment with multiple open roles simultaneously

Pay and benefits

- Meaningful stock option plan offered (included in the majority of full time offers).

title: Business Development Representative (BDR) — End-of-Studies Internship
description:
Our team shared’s mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect 

We believe healthcare shouldn’t be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better.

Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care.

Already trusted by 3500+ providers, we’re transforming the patient–provider relationship, one call at a time.

Want to shape the future of healthcare?

Join us ! 

- Discover our company culture and values 

- Here is a product Demo 

- Meet the team 

- Article on our seed round of 5,5M$ 

Your mission 
As a Business Development Representative intern, you'll be on the front line of our growth engine. Your job is to generate qualified meetings with healthcare leaders who are overwhelmed by missed calls and inefficiencies, and show them how Vocca can change the game.

You'll hunt, qualify, and open doors so our Account Executives can close. You'll learn how to prospect like a pro, pitch like a consultant, and build the foundations of a sales career — with the goal of joining us full-time at the end of your internship.

Expected outcomes 

1 month: 

- Master our pitch, our CRM, and our outbound playbook.

- Book your first qualified meetings with healthcare prospects.

3 months: 

- Consistently hit monthly meeting targets through a mix of outbound calls, emails, and LinkedIn outreach.

- Own inbound qualification: every lead gets a fast, thoughtful response.

- Share field insights with Sales & Marketing to improve targeting.

End of internship (5-6 months): 

- Be performing at or near full quota, ready to hit the ground running as a full-time BDR.

- Have tested and proposed new outbound tactics (copy, sequences, channels).

- Convert to a full-time contract (CDI) if you perform well.

Who you are 
This is for you if:

- You're ambitious, competitive, and hungry to prove yourself.

- You thrive on challenges and don't shy away from the grind of outbound sales.

- You have excellent communication skills: clear, confident, and persuasive.

- You're coachable and eager to learn: you want feedback, you act on it fast.

- You're resilient: every "no" just brings you closer to a "yes."

- You're in your final year of business school, engineering school, or equivalent, looking for an end-of-studies internship (convention de stage required), and open to converting to full-time.

It's a plus if you:

- Have experience in sales, retail, hospitality, or any role where convincing and resilience were key.

- Already used Attio (CRM).

Career perspectives 

- Learn modern sales from the ground up in a fast-growing AI startup.

- Be coached directly by the founders & early sales leaders.

- Fast-track to a full-time BDR role at the end of your internship, with a clear path: SDR → AE → Sales Leader.

Hiring Process 
Intro interview (20 min) — with our Recruiter, to get to know each other and confirm alignment.

- HM interview (20 min) — with one person from the Sales Team, to get to know each other and confirm alignment.

- Situational interview (45 min) — with 2 sales from the team: targeted questions + sales role-play + debrief.

- Founders interview (30 min) — with the Head of Sales, to discuss vision, culture, and ambition.

- Offer! 🎉

We aim to keep the process within 30 days . You’ll receive continuous feedback throughout.

Why should you join Vocca? 

- An entrepreneurial adventure , with a supportive, high-energy, execution-focused team

- A product already live , with delighted customers in a fast-growing market (healthcare automation, voice AI)

- A true scaling phase , with everything still to build

- Real responsibilities from day one

We hire people, not roles. 

If you're excited about our opportunities but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success. If you identify yourself as a woman : Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

title: Clinical Data Manager RWD/RWE
description:
À propos de Lifen

Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales peuvent transformer le système de santé, à condition qu’elles soient accessibles. Mieux les faire circuler, c’est réduire la charge administrative, mieux coordonner les soins et accélérer la recherche clinique.

Depuis 2015, nous développons des solutions qui aident les professionnels de santé à partager les informations médicales et les chercheurs à exploiter des données de santé. Plus de 150 personnes travaillent chez Lifen, depuis nos bureaux et à distance. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé en France.

Notre équipe

L’équipe Clinical Ops intervient au cœur de nos projets de recherche clinique fondés sur des données de santé. Elle transforme des documents médicaux en données structurées, nécessaires à la constitution de cohortes patients et à la préparation des exports utilisés dans nos projets de recherche.

Aujourd’hui, l’équipe structure environ 100 à 200 cas patients par semaine . Notre ambition : tripler cette capacité dans les 9 prochains mois, tout en maintenant un haut niveau de qualité des données.

Pour y parvenir, nous cherchons une personne capable de reprendre le management de l’équipe, mais surtout de piloter le flux de production, d’anticiper la charge et de porter une démarche d’amélioration continue avec les équipes Produit, IA et Engineering.

C’est un rôle à la croisée du management opérationnel, de la RWD et de l’amélioration de processus .

Ce que tu feras chez nous

Ta première mission sera de reprendre le pilotage de la production des cohortes afin d’en améliorer simultanément la qualité, la capacité de traitement et le niveau d’automatisation .

Concrètement, tu seras amené·e à :

- Manager et faire grandir l’équipe Clinical Ops, en donnant un cadre clair aux priorités et en organisant l’activité quotidienne.

- Anticiper la charge et piloter la capacité de production afin de limiter les bottlenecks et de mieux absorber les variations de volume.

- Construire les outils de pilotage nécessaires pour avoir une vision fine du flux : volumes de patients, capacité de traitement, taux d’erreur, points de blocage et charge de l’équipe.

- Construire et orchestrer une roadmap d’amélioration continue permettant progressivement d’augmenter la capacité de traitement.

- Porter cette roadmap auprès des équipes Produit, IA et Engineering : rendre les besoins opérationnels visibles, suivre les livrables R&D et créer le rythme nécessaire pour que les améliorations soient effectivement délivrées.

- Garantir la qualité des cohortes et contribuer à la préparation des exports de données nécessaires aux projets de recherche.

Ce que nous attendrons de toi

Dans les premiers mois, nous attendrons de toi que tu développes une compréhension très fine du flux Clinical Ops : où se trouvent les blocages, comment évolue la charge et quels leviers permettent réellement d'améliorer la production.

Ton succès se mesurera notamment à ta capacité à mettre en place un pilotage fiable de l’activité, à réduire les erreurs et les bottlenecks et à créer, avec les équipes Produit et R&D, un rythme d’amélioration continue suffisamment soutenu pour accompagner notre changement d’échelle.

À horizon 9 mois, l’objectif est clair : passer d’environ 100–200 à 300–600 cas patients structurés par semaine, sans multiplier les ressources par trois. 

Ce que nous recherchons

Must-have

Nous chercherons en priorité trois éléments dans ton parcours :

- Une expérience réussie en startup ou scale-up , dans un environnement où les process, outils et responsabilités restaient à construire.

- Une expérience concrète de la Real-World Data / Real-World Evidence , idéalement autour de la constitution ou de l'exploitation de cohortes patients.

- Un background santé ou scientifique te permettant de comprendre les enjeux liés aux données médicales et à la recherche clinique.

Nous attendons également :

- Une expérience confirmée de management d’équipe opérationnelle .

- Une expérience de structuration et de pilotage d’une activité complexe à partir de données et de KPI.

- Une capacité à passer d’un problème opérationnel très concret à un plan d’amélioration structuré.

- Une expérience de collaboration étroite avec des équipes Produit, Data/IA ou Engineering .

- Une capacité à faire avancer une roadmap transverse et à créer de l’accountability autour des livrables.

Nice-to-have

- Un parcours en data management, biostatistiques, épidémiologie ou dans un domaine scientifique proche.

- Une expérience de structuration de registres, bases de données de santé ou cohortes RWD.

- Une familiarité avec les enjeux de recherche clinique et les interactions avec les autorités de santé.

- Une bonne compréhension des usages de l’IA et de l’ingénierie appliqués aux données de santé.

Ta manière de travailler

Tu as une vraie “just do it mentality” : face à un problème imparfaitement cadré, tu commences par comprendre les faits, tu structures le problème et tu mets rapidement en place les premières solutions.

Tu es particulièrement à l’aise dans les environnements où il faut créer les outils plutôt que simplement les utiliser. Si le dashboard dont tu as besoin pour piloter ton équipe n’existe pas, tu es capable de le définir et de le mettre en place.

Tu es structuré·e et organisé·e, mais pas bureaucratique. Tu sais entrer suffisamment dans le détail du flux pour comprendre les problèmes réels, tout en gardant une vision d’ensemble et en priorisant ce qui aura le plus d’impact.

Enfin, tu sais faire avancer des équipes sur lesquelles tu n’as pas nécessairement d’autorité hiérarchique. Tu rends les problèmes visibles, explicites les priorités et crées le rythme nécessaire pour transformer les décisions en améliorations concrètes.

Nos valeurs

Embrace Complexity — Tu aimes comprendre un flux de données complexe, en identifier les points de rupture et transformer cette complexité en décisions concrètes.

Bienveillance — Tu accompagnes une équipe au quotidien avec exigence, écoute et clarté.

Real Impact — Tu améliores la qualité et la disponibilité des données qui permettent de faire avancer des projets de recherche clinique.

Process de recrutement

Échange de préqualification avec Laura, Talent Acquisition Manager, 30 minutes. Nous faisons connaissance, revenons sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les grandes lignes du poste. C’est aussi le moment de répondre à tes premières questions sur Lifen, l’équipe et le contexte.

Entretien avec le VP Reasearch, 60 minutes. Nous revenons plus en détail sur ton parcours, ton expérience en RWD et en constitution de cohortes, ainsi que sur ton expérience de management et de pilotage d’activités opérationnelles. L’objectif est aussi de comprendre la manière dont tu structures et fais évoluer une organisation dans un environnement en croissance.

Use Case avec des membres des équipes Clinical Ops et Produit, 60 minutes. À partir de situations concrètes, nous échangeons sur ta manière de structurer une cohorte RWD, d’analyser des problématiques opérationnelles et de construire des plans d’amélioration. Ce sera également l’occasion d’aborder la manière dont tu gères les enjeux humains et la collaboration avec des équipes transverses.

Cultural alignment avec deux membres de Lifen, 45 minutes en visio. Ce temps permettra d’échanger sur ta façon de travailler, ton niveau d’autonomie, la collaboration au quotidien et l’adéquation avec nos valeurs.

title: Operations Manager, Offer Operations
description:
At Joko, our mission is to we help consumers save time and money when shopping online or in-store. 

Founded in Paris, Joko is a tech company and certified B Corp with over 120 talents across Paris, Barcelona, and New York (and beyond). More than 6 million users already save money every day at 10,000+ merchants with Joko. 

From cashback and automatic coupons to price alerts, we've kept expanding our products to make shopping smarter. Today, Joko is an AI shopping app: with Juno, our shopping assistant, users can find the right product at the best price in only a few seconds, with recommendations that get sharper the more they use it.

Having reached profitability in our core market, we’re now scaling globally, with a strong focus on the US. 

It’s still day 1, come build the future of shopping with us! 

🦾 Our Offer Operations team 

Joko helps millions of users earn cashback automatically, whether they shop online through affiliate links, activate coupons, or pay in-store with their linked bank card. Behind each of these experiences, there's an operational engine that needs to work flawlessly: transactions must be tracked, cashback must be caught, offers must be reliable, and merchants must perform as expected. When this engine breaks, users don't get paid — and trust erodes fast.

Offer Operations owns that engine. The team's mission is to guarantee the reliability and continuous improvement of Joko's core monetization mechanics — across affiliate tracking, coupons, card-linked bank integrations, gift cards, and merchant performance. It's a technical, data-heavy, high-stakes scope that sits right at the heart of what makes Joko's product work.

🎯 What you will do 

As an Operations Manager, your main mission is to own one of the processes that decides whether millions of Joko users actually get the cashback they're owed. You'll report to David Le Pahun , our Offer Operations Lead. The role blends four things: analysing data, designing how the process should work, solving problems with AI, technologies or in the last resort outsourcing, and managing projects.

- Analyse data. You'll build the dashboards that tell you — and everyone else — whether your part of the system is healthy: how many transactions are being correctly tracked and rewarded, what's silently breaking down, whether user experience is suffering.

- Design the process. You decide how merchants get set up on our platform: their cashback rate, which purchases qualify, how we connect to their systems. A lot of this doesn't have a playbook yet — you'll be writing a good chunk of it as you go.

- Solve problems with technology. A merchant might be showing users a coupon that doesn't actually pay out. A batch of card purchases might not match cleanly to any merchant we track. You'll dig into why, then fix it choosing the right solution for it: automating it with AI, improving one of our internal tools (built on Retool) and if a human is required, you'll build the right playbook to outsource it.

- Manage outsourced resources. You'll manage the outsourced team members who help you operate at scale — briefing them, training them, checking their work is actually good — while juggling several of these issues at once and deciding what matters most.

- Partner cross-functionally. With Product & Engineering when the fix is structural, and with the commercial team when it's really about a merchant relationship.

👀 Who we're looking for 

- Experience: around 2–5 years of experience, ideally with exposure to Operations, Product, or a technical/data-driven environment.

- AI-native: you genuinely believe in what AI can do, and you already use it as part of how you work — not as a buzzword, but as a real way to automate the repetitive parts of your job and move faster on the rest.

- Ops mindset: you think in systems — monitoring → detection → investigation → resolution → prevention. You instinctively look for what can break and build safeguards so it doesn't happen again.

- Tech acumen: you're comfortable in a technical environment — tracking, APIs, integrations — and can hold your own in a conversation with Engineering.

- Analytical skills: you're data-driven and comfortable navigating dashboards, investigating anomalies, and making decisions based on metrics.

- Attention to detail: the devil is in the details, and you have a talent for spotting flaws where others don't.

- Communication: clear written and verbal communication skills; you're not afraid to defend your decisions with demanding stakeholders (including merchants and the outsourced teams you'll be directing).

- Education: Top-tier engineering or business school background. International experience and a double degree are a clear plus.

- Languages: fluent in written and spoken English. Mastering French is not required.

💎 Our perks 

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only) 

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

- Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

- Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

- 💸 Top-market compensation

- 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

- 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

- 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

- 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

- 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

- …and much more, check the full list here !

🤝 Our hiring process 

- Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

- Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

- Step 2 – Role-specific assessments 

- For non-engineering roles : A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

- For engineering roles : A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

- Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

- References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

☕ You may also be invited for coffee with team members to get a feel for our culture.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous 

En tant qu’ingénieur(e) de recherche en intelligence artificielle appliquée à la vision industrielle 3D, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche, innovation technologique et transfert vers l’industrie, affecté(e) au Centre Fayol de l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne.

Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol.

Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 

📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles.

Au sein de ce centre de recherche pluridisciplinaire (plus de 80 personnes), reconnu pour son expertise en IA, systèmes cyber-physiques et sciences des données, vous contribuerez à des projets de R&D à fort impact pour l’industrie du futur. Le centre s’appuie notamment sur sa plateformes technologiques IT'M Factory et est un acteur-clé de l'enseignement et de l'innovation au sein de l’Institut Mines-Télécom.

Dans le cadre du projet régional DIGIMAN3D, financé par la Région Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, ce recrutement vise à développer et expérimenter une solution de contrôle dimensionnel 3D en ligne, basée sur l’acquisition de données 3D et l’intelligence artificielle, pour le contrôle automatisé de pièces mécaniques de précision en conditions industrielles.

title: Endear - Product Designer
description:
Location: Remote, US-based
Team: Product & Design — IRL
Type: Full-Time, Employee
Compensation: $100K–$129K base
Target Start: January 2027 or earlier

Our Story 

At Endear, we’re building the modern CRM for retail teams — starting with the frontline.

Our software helps retail teams build stronger customer relationships through thoughtful, intuitive technology. From clienteling and customer capture to appointments and in-store experiences, Endear gives brands the tools they need to create more personal interactions and drive measurable growth.

We work with brands like Allbirds, Reformation, and Alo Yoga, and we’re continuing to evolve Endear into an increasingly AI-first product built around how modern retail teams actually work.

Position Overview 

We’re looking for a Product Designer to join our IRL (in real life) team, which owns the in-store side of Endear — including appointments, events, customer check-ins, and the administrative experiences behind those workflows.

You’ll design for store associates and managers running clienteling day to day, as well as admin users who help shape how those teams operate and manage their workflows.

In this role, you’ll own features and projects from understanding the problem through research, testing, iteration, and production-ready design, while partnering closely with our Head of Product Design on vision and direction.

The IRL roadmap is early. Many of these features don’t exist yet, so you’ll be defining problems through research before designing solutions.

This role is well suited for someone comfortable creating clarity when the solution isn’t obvious.

What You’ll Accomplish 

In your first 6 months, you’ll… 

- Take ownership of IRL features from discovery through production-ready design

- Build a strong understanding of how store associates, managers, and admin users work within Endear

- Run research from early discovery through usability testing

- Design complete, accessible product experiences, including loading, empty, error, permission, and other key states.

- Partner closely with Product and Engineering to shape solutions early in the process

- Use customer insight and data to inform design decisions and iteration

In your first year, you’ll… 

- Build deeper ownership across the IRL product

- Deliver product experiences that improve how retail teams manage clienteling and in-store workflows

- Build a strong rhythm of discovery, testing, and continuous learning

- Strengthen your collaboration across Design, Product, and Engineering

- Demonstrate clear user and business impact through the work you ship

You’ll Thrive in This Role If… 

- You enjoy taking ownership of a feature while collaborating closely on the broader vision and direction

- You’re comfortable with ambiguity and zero-to-one product work

- You naturally think beyond the happy path and account for edge cases and complete product states

- You care about creating accessible experiences and solving the right problem, not just creating polished UI

- You enjoy working closely with Product and Engineering throughout the design process

- You’re comfortable using research, data, and customer feedback to guide decisions

- You move quickly, seek feedback, and iterate based on what you learn

- You’re curious about designing for AI

You Have Experience With 

- 2–5 years working in product design

- Independently owning features from discovery through implementation, with support on vision and direction

- Running user research from discovery through usability testing

- Translating broad or ambiguous problems into clear product solutions

- Working closely with Design, Product, and Engineering teams

- Designing complex, accessible workflows and accounting for loading, empty, error, and permission states

- Using qualitative and quantitative data to inform design decisions

- Building within established design patterns while knowing when something needs to evolve

- Using AI tools as part of your workflow and applying judgment to AI-generated output

- A portfolio that demonstrates strong product thinking and execution, and where you can articulate the impact of your work, with data where you had access to it

Align With What We Value 

At Endear, we live by five core principles. Here’s how they translate into what we’re looking for in this role:

- Customer First: You start by understanding the people using the product, run thoughtful research, and use what you learn to shape better experiences.

- Take Ownership: You take responsibility for your features, follow through on the details, and care about the quality of what ships.

- Enable Autonomy: You communicate clearly, collaborate early, and give Product and Engineering the context they need to make strong decisions together.

- Under Promise, Over Deliver: You set realistic expectations, think through the details, and deliver complete, production-ready work.

- Innovate & Deliver Value Quickly: You’re comfortable experimenting, using AI and other tools thoughtfully, and moving quickly without sacrificing sound product judgment.

About the Team 

Endear’s product organization is structured across three product teams: AI, IRL, and Core Flows, with one designer dedicated to each.

As the IRL designer, you’ll work closely with a Product Manager and 2–3 Engineers while also being part of Endear’s three-person design team. You’ll report to the Head of Product Design, who will provide vision, direction, mentorship, and support as you grow in the role.

You’ll partner most closely with:

- Head of Product Design: vision, direction, mentorship, feedback, and design leadership

- Product Team: roadmap alignment, priorities, customer needs, and business context

- Engineering Team: feasibility, implementation, and iteration

You’ll have access to mentorship, an education budget, and support around Endear’s AI processes to help you continue developing your craft and expanding how you use AI in your work.

We’re a small team with big ambitions — collaborative, customer-obsessed, and deeply excited about the problems we’re solving in retail.

Our Hiring Process 

- Recruiter Screen

- Behavioral Interview with the Hiring Manager

- Team Portfolio Review with Design, Product + Engineering

- Final leadership conversation

- Offer 🎉

Compensation & Benefits 

- Base Salary: $100K–$129K

- Fully remote, US-based team

- Comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, vision)

- Co-working or home office stipend

- Flexible PTO and unlimited vacation

- Education and learning support

- Opportunity to shape foundational product work in a transformative industry

Location: This role is remote and US-based. Our full team comes together for an all-team standup every Monday at 8:00 AM Pacific, so you’ll need to be available at that time.

Apply Even If You Don’t Check Every Box 

If this role excites you but you’re unsure if you meet every requirement, reach out anyway. No retail or e-commerce background is required. We care about your product thinking, skills, motivation, and how you approach problems more than we do about perfect resumes.

- Java (recent versions)

- SQL

- Cloud platforms

- Microservices architecture

Languages 

- French : Full professional proficiency

title: Chief of staff/GTM to Raphaël Vullierme (Hexa Partner)
description:
About Hexa 

Hexa (formerly eFounders) gives entrepreneurs the best chances to build outstanding companies.

We are a pioneering, world-leading startup studio born in Europe that designs, builds and launches category-defining startups. We are today recognized as one of the best venture studios in the world, with a track record comparable to tier-1 VC funds.

We have created 60+ companies (including 3 unicorns) with a combined valuation of over $5 billion, among them Aircall, Spendesk, Front, Swan and Yousign. We are passionate about B2B software, particularly AI-native and agentic SaaS, fintech, climate tech, etc.

Hexa is in full growth mode, with three early-stage activities: our Ventures programs Hexa Start and Hexa Sprint which help entrepreneurs go from zero to one, and a PE program, Hexa Scale, which takes majority stakes in existing startups and pushes them to new thresholds.

The AI-native vertical at Hexa: WTF 

WTF (“Walk The Frontier”) is leading Hexa’s effort at the frontier of AI model and led by Raphaël Vullierme, a repeat founder who built Luko France #1 online home insurer now part of Allianz, previous CEO of OpenJet an uber for private aviation, and started out launching ventures at Rocket Internet. We build companies with Europe’s best founders, global from day zero, with offices in Paris and San Francisco.

We’re building across three theses: 

- Physical AI / Defense / Infrastructure to answer European sovereignty need. 
This means we are building real technology with very fast time to market and value by moving atoms and not only bits. 

- AI is the buyer. 
Buying decision are being taken by Agent or from an AI analysis. AI process more data and is less irrational / emotional than human. Cost to compare, switch, quote is trending to 0. This will have an enormous impact on market, what get sold or buy way beyond retail and ecommerce. This will much more transformative to the economy than the efficiency gains most AI startup currently focus on. 

- Financial Services & Regulated business. 
Raphael was CEO of a full stack & regulated insurer. AI is eating the moat of large Financial institution and we are working to re-invent risk and capital is being moved and allocated. 

We started in Jan 26 and so far WTF has had a very prolific year building 3 companies. The 2 first raised large seed 4 from TopTier VC 4month after the inception in 2 very different vertical. 

- WaniWani Agentic Commerce Infrastructure for financial services. Leading Banks, Insurers such as Chubb, Satender, BPI, Axa, Generali runs their AI distribution (selling insurance/mortgage to AI agent - on chatGPT/Gemini…) on Waniwani platform. Several million in ARR reach on Year 1 with US being fastest growing market.

- Pelagon is building a foundational acoustic AI model for autonomous maritime protection, deployed across a distributed network of underwater and surface vectors to give European navies real-time understanding of underwater threats. Working with several EU navies and deployed commercially.

It is a rare role to build category-defining companies learn how they get built, from the inside, at the frontier of AI. High intensity team, high challenge, high worker and learned.

The mission 

We’re looking for a Chief of Staff to be the execution backbone of WTF: right hand to Raphaël and to our founders, bringing an operator’s rigor to fast-moving, still-forming teams. The role splits into two:

80% - real company-building 

Hands-on helping our founders operate their companies across the whole lifecycle, from early discovery and scoping a new idea, through founder search, to building and scaling once it’s live.

- Go-to-market, your main focus: you own GTM for each company: positioning, first customers, sales, pricing, go-to-market experiments, and the tools, automations and trackers needed to run them. Hexa’s central pool covers product and design; GTM sits with you. You are part of the company and our growth depend on you.

- In the operational rhythm of each company: weekly kick-offs, product meetings, end-of-week recaps. You own the cadence, objectives set, notes written, decisions tracked, and leverage AI so we focus our time on building and selling not writing down plans.

- The founders’ first port of call on anything outside their own scope, and the interface between the ventures and the rest of Hexa (Finance, Legal, Talent, Comms), pulling in the right resource when a project needs it.

20% - studio operations 

- How we run as a studio: keeping the machine sharp and the founder pipeline full.

- Discovery transforming new ideas into tangible opportunities: discovery outreach and meeting, market sizing, value chain, positioning, the opportunity note that gets a project greenlit.

- Growing the founder pipeline: working with the Talent team on the sourcing strategy for each new project, gathering top talent in the industry and making WTF visible to the best potential founders and ecosystem players.

- Building visibility: working with the brand team on Raphaël’s and the studio’s reputation.

- Improving how the studio (and Hexa) runs: sharpening shared AI agent and tooling (GTM ex: github repo), playbooks and best practice (ex: grokbot rollout), and reusable systems that make the studio & Hexa as a whole compound over time.

Who we’re looking for .

- 2 to 4 years of experience as founder, go-to-market, growth, operations or even engineering in tech company/ecossystem. This is your shot to build real things, not assist. How you execute and you track executing matters more than the title on your resume.

- A builder. You’ve been hands-on inside an early-stage startup, or founded something yourself, and you build things: automations, tools, dashboards, experiments.

- A genuine go-to-market appetite: you’re not afraid to reach out cold, and you like the hands-on part of landing the first customers. You will meet real people and sell while being nobody for them.

- High agency. You’re the person who figures it out and ships, without waiting to be told how.

- Hard worker and hungry: you want to be part of building great companies, and you bring energy, hard work and rigor to it.

- AI nerd: you use AI tools on a daily basis and constantly test switch to better setup.

- Comfortable being in front of people: reaching out to founders, hosting events, representing the studio.

- Working in English 

Recruitment process 

- First call with Louise (current GTM lead): introduction to Hexa, WTF, check on cultural fit.

- Interview with Raphaël: mutual introduction, deep dive into the role and how we work.

- Case study: an exercise inspired by our real work.

- Cultural fit interview with Matthieu (CEO) and Camille (VP Talent)

What we offer

- 53-56K + 20% "intéressement": 63K-67K total comp

- Direct equity in the studio's companies

- Opportunity to invest in Hexa portfolio startups at a preferential rate

- Swile meal card

- 8 to 12 RTT days per year

- Mobility budget: €500/year for green transportation (bike, metro, electric scooter)

- Health insurance with 50% coverage for you and your family

- 1% Holiday bonus
